audit_findings.title: The parent-level claim may be mixed with consolidated OpCo cash or cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: at least $42.4 million, or $1.20 per unit, computed
audit_findings.evidence: Westlake's retained interest of 77.2 % is recorded as noncontrolling interest in the Partnership's consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-bridge error is demonstrated. The $92.898 million bridge equals consolidated cash of $49.321 million plus the $43.577 million investment-management receivable. Corporate total assets are only $37.972 million, so at least $54.926 million belongs to OpCo; the 77.2% NCI share of that minimum is $42.4 million and cannot belong to WLKP common units. The extent of any similar contamination in historical OE remains unresolved. The demonstrated bridge overstatement is large enough to reduce every scenario by at least $1.20 per unit and affect the margin-of-safety conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level cash and investment-management schedules at June 30, 2026, add only WLKP corporate cash plus 22.8% of OpCo cash, and rerun all per-unit values and buy-below figures. Separately trace every historical D&A, disposition and capital-expenditure adjustment to WLKP or its 22.8% OpCo interest.

audit_findings.title: Recurring turnaround reinvestment may have been added back without an economic replacement deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.9 million for 2025, computed as 22.8% of the filed $39.017 million normalized turnaround reserve; 14.3% of the $62.1 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: OE anchor and projected operating cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: The costs of the turnaround are deferred when incurred at the time of the turnaround and amortized (within depreciation and amortization) on a straight-line basis until the next planned turnaround, which typically ranges from five to eight years .
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated by the supplied computation. The $62.1 million anchor closely reconciles to parent-attributable net income plus 22.8% of consolidated D&A and dispositions less 22.8% of maintenance capex, without a separate turnaround reserve. Turnaround amortization is included in the D&A add-back, while the filing identifies recurring five-to-eight-year turnarounds and separately deducts a $39.017 million contribution to turnaround reserves in its distributable-cash-flow calculation. The corresponding $8.9 million common claim is material relative to anchor OE. Contractual recovery of turnaround spending through revenue does not eliminate the reinvestment deduction because that recovery is already reflected in earnings.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year with a separately identified actual or normalized turnaround cash deduction, reconcile it to deferred-turnaround additions, amortization and reserve contributions, prevent double counting with maintenance capex, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The perpetual forecast extends far beyond the secured term of the core related-party economics
audit_findings.magnitude: computed terminal-value PV exposure of $306.0 million bear, $433.9 million base and $495.8 million bull, equal to 46.3%-50.9% of operating PV; actual adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: growth assumptions, explicit-period OE and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.
audit_findings.explanation: The contract expiry is demonstrated, while adverse renewal or repricing is an unresolved possibility. The cost-plus Ethylene Sales Agreement is secured only through December 31, 2027, yet substantially all forecast years and the perpetual terminal value presume continuing economics. Because roughly half of operating value is terminal value alone, termination, merchant-market exposure or weaker renewal terms are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The exact adjustment cannot be established without post-2027 contract scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the explicit forecast and terminal value under probability-weighted post-2027 cases covering renewal on current terms, lower margin or cost recovery, and termination with merchant economics; document the probabilities and resulting OE in each case.

audit_findings.title: Incentive distribution rights are a participating equity claim absent from the common-unit denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the first threshold is $1.2938 quarterly or $5.1752 annually per unit, equivalent to $182.5 million annually across 35.260894 million units, versus filed annual distributions of about $66.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: equity allocation, terminal value and potential share dilution
audit_findings.evidence: Incentive distribution rights represent the right to receive increasing percentages (15.0%, 25.0% and 50.0%) of quarterly distributions from operating surplus after the target distribution levels have been achieved.
audit_findings.explanation: No present IDR payment is omitted: the current $0.4714 quarterly distribution is only 36% of the first threshold. Even $66.5 million growing at 5% for ten years would reach only about $108.3 million, still below the $182.5 million first-threshold scale. However, the valuation is perpetual, distributions were not forecast explicitly, and positive terminal growth can eventually activate the IDRs or permit a reset that issues units. The record therefore shows a possible common-equity claim but does not establish whether its present value is material.
audit_findings.action: Build a quarterly distribution waterfall from forecast available cash, test all three IDR tiers throughout the explicit and terminal periods, model any permitted reset-unit issuance, and rerun common-unit value if any threshold is crossed.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded asset-retirement obligations could be a senior economic liability
audit_findings.mechanism: equity bridge and future OE or capital expenditures
audit_findings.evidence: However, no asset retirement obligations have been recognized because the fair value of the conditional legal obligation cannot be measured due to the indeterminate settlement date of the obligation.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of conditional legal obligations is demonstrated, but neither settlement timing nor fair value is measurable from the filing. Consequently, the record cannot establish materiality. Any residual obligation not covered by enforceable Westlake indemnities would consume cash ahead of common units and is omitted from both the bridge and historical OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain site-level engineering cost estimates, expected settlement dates and probabilities; determine the legal obligor and the scope, duration and collectability of Westlake indemnities; allocate any OpCo residual economically between WLKP and the 77.2% NCI, discount it, and rerun the bridge if material.
